source_refs.note: Topic 15.4 with the For Information box on the neuromuscular junction (PDF 33).

blocks.text: The junction between axon terminal of one neuron and the dendrites of other neurons, or effector cells (of muscle or gland) is called a synapse. At a synapse, the two neurons or a neuron and a cell are not in direct contact. Rather, there is a fluid-filled gap between them, called a synaptic cleft. The neuron whose axon transmits action potentials towards synapse is the presynaptic neuron. The neuron or cell on the other side of the synapse is the postsynaptic cell.

blocks.title: For Information
blocks.text: The synapse between a motor neuron and a muscle fibre is also called neuro-muscular junction.
